The prior iid theorem, Stage161 and Stage162 belong to their existing provenance and were not rewritten.

## Model and observer

Let H_n be a finite positive-weight labeled prefix tree, depth n=0,...,N. Both hypotheses P,Q assign strictly positive probabilities to each admissible prefix and share support. At a live history h, one common behavioral policy chooses D_P (stop and decide P), D_Q (stop and decide Q), or C (continue; illegal at horizon N). Upon C, successor ha has probabilities p(a|h)=P(ha)/P(h) and q(a|h)=Q(ha)/Q(h), independent of other past policy randomization conditional on the full h. The first observation may be compulsory. Let T_n:H_n→X_n be a deterministic statistic.

The four target observables are e_P=P(decide Q), e_Q=Q(decide P), t_P=E_P[tau], t_Q=E_Q[tau]. A stronger target is all statistic-indexed, two-hypothesis live/action masses. Neither target includes all ordered source labels or an unknown future native state update.

## Theorem A — LR + P-only lumpability yields exact two-hypothesis Markovization

Suppose (LR) for each n and x, Q(h)/P(h)=ell_n(x)>0 for every h with T_n(h)=x. Suppose (P-LUMP), for n<N,

kappa^P_n(h,y) := sum_{a:T_{n+1}(ha)=y} p(a|h) = K^P_n(x,y),

depends on h only through x=T_n(h). Then:

1. Q-lumpability follows automatically, with

   K^Q_n(x,y) = [ell_{n+1}(y)/ell_n(x)] K^P_n(x,y).                  (A1)

2. Every full-history randomized stopping/decision policy pi admits an (n,T_n)-Markov policy with the same P- and Q-indexed live/action masses at each statistic state, and therefore the same four observables.

3. The exact four-observer attainable region is the linear image of a finite nonnegative occupation-flow polytope; there is no full-history variable in this polytope.

**Proof of 1.** For each edge h→ha from statistic state x to y, use (LR) at both ends:

q(a|h) = Q(ha)/Q(h) = [ell_{n+1}(y)/ell_n(x)] P(ha)/P(h)
       = [ell_{n+1}(y)/ell_n(x)] p(a|h).

Summing over edges into y gives (A1). Thus the apparently two-sided hypothesis-specific future-kernel assumption in the new research question is redundant: one-sided lumpability suffices when (LR) holds at *both* consecutive layers.

**Proof of 2.** Write s_pi(h) for the probability of surviving to h given the full observation prefix and pi_a(h) for the survival-conditioned action probability. They depend on the common policy, not on the hypothesis. Let

mu_P(h)=P(h)s_pi(h),  mu_Q(h)=Q(h)s_pi(h)=ell_n(T_n(h))mu_P(h).

For a state x define m_n(x)=sum_{T_n(h)=x}mu_P(h) and u_{n,x,a}=sum_{T_n(h)=x}mu_P(h)pi_a(h). Define bar_pi_a(n,x)=u_{n,x,a}/m_n(x) for positive m_n(x); use an arbitrary legal distribution at unreachable states.

At the root the aggregated P-live masses agree. If they agree at depth n, the P-action masses agree by construction; Q-action masses equal ell_n(x) times these P masses by (LR). Under either the original or the averaged policy, (P-LUMP) gives the next P-live mass

m_{n+1}(y)=sum_x K^P_n(x,y)u_{n,x,C}.

Induction proves equality at every layer; fiberwise (LR) yields Q equality. All observer sums are therefore equal. No claim is made that hidden-history mass distributions inside an x-fiber coincide.

**Proof of 3.** Introduce u_{n,x,D_P},u_{n,x,D_Q},u_{n,x,C}≥0 (omit C at N) with m_n(x)=sum_a u_{n,x,a}; root m_0=1; and the only transition constraints

m_{n+1}(y)=sum_x K^P_n(x,y)u_{n,x,C}.

The exact linear readouts are

e_P=sum_{n,x}u_{n,x,D_Q};       e_Q=sum_{n,x}ell_n(x)u_{n,x,D_P};
t_P=sum_{n<N,x}u_{n,x,C};      t_Q=sum_{n<N,x}ell_n(x)u_{n,x,C}.

Every T-Markov policy induces feasible flows, and every feasible flow induces a T-Markov policy by dividing each nonnegative action mass by its live mass. Q-conservation follows from (A1). This establishes an exact polytope description, not a relaxation. QED.

**Limits:** The two models must have the same positive branch support; the statistic's LR must be constant at *every* layer. Actions only choose stop/continue here. A model with several action-dependent continuation kernels requires action-indexed conditions; a physical/X6 update is not supplied by this theorem.

## Theorem B — policy-dependent pushforward preservation is strictly weaker

Fix one full-history policy pi under (LR), form its fiber-averaged bar_pi, and evaluate their own full-history P-live masses mu_P^pi and mu_P^bar. Without assuming P-LUMP, define

Phi_n^pi(x,y)=sum_{h:T_n(h)=x}mu_P^pi(h)pi_C(h)kappa^P_n(h,y),
Phi_n^bar(x,y)=bar_pi_C(n,x)sum_{h:T_n(h)=x}mu_P^bar(h)kappa^P_n(h,y).

If Phi_n^pi(x,y)=Phi_n^bar(x,y) for every layer, x and y, then the two policies have the same P- and Q-tagged statistic occupation/action masses and four observers.

**Proof.** Base masses agree. Fiber averaging and equality of aggregated P-live mass give equal P-action masses; (LR) gives equal Q-action masses. Phi equality supplies equality of next P-live aggregate masses. On each edge x→y, Q transition mass equals [ell_{n+1}(y)/ell_n(x)] times P transition mass, so the aggregate Q flow is ell_{n+1}(y) times the aggregate P next mass. Induct. QED.

**Quantifier order:** P-LUMP is a history-uniform condition implying *for every* pi that the averaging construction succeeds, and gives a kernel-defined occupation LP. The Phi condition is checked for *one given pi and its actually induced bar_pi*, with both complete hidden-history distributions. It can hold even if P-LUMP fails (e.g. pi already depends only on T), but it is not a policy-independent closed transition kernel and does not prove preservation for all pi. Nor is it claimed necessary for the four scalars alone; it is an exact sufficient test for the finer statistic-indexed action flows.

## Positive-rational counterexample — LR holds, P-LUMP fails, all-four preservation fails

Take N=2, compulsory first observation P(a)=Q(a)=P(b)=Q(b)=1/2. The second-step positive-rational laws are

| h | P(0|h) | P(1|h) | Q(0|h) | Q(1|h) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| a | 3/4 | 1/4 | 1/4 | 3/4 |
| b | 1/2 | 1/2 | 1/2 | 1/2 |

Let T_1(a)=T_1(b)=x, while T_2 retains the full ordered path a0,a1,b0,b1. LR is constant at the only nonsingleton fiber: ell_1(x)=1; T_2 fibers are singletons. P-LUMP fails because the next-T=a0 probability is 3/4 after a and zero after b (likewise Q nonlumpable).

A full-history policy continues only after a, decides P at a0 and Q at a1; after b it stops at n=1 and chooses P/Q with fair private randomization. Direct exact calculation gives

(e_P,e_Q,t_P,t_Q)=(3/8,3/8,3/2,3/2),  e_P+e_Q=3/4.       (B1)

Every T-Markov policy has the same continue probability c at the indistinguishable depth-one state x. Matching t_P=t_Q=3/2 requires c=1/2. For any such policy the total error is at least the uninformative stopped mass plus the optimal continuing Bayes overlap:

e_P+e_Q ≥ (1-c) + c sum_{w∈{a0,a1,b0,b1}}min(P(w),Q(w))
         = (1-c)+3c/4 = 1-c/4 = 7/8 > 3/4.                (B2)

This is a strict *four-observer* obstruction, not just an unpreserved state occupancy. (B2) is attained by taking c=1/2, fair stop decisions and optimal terminal decisions, giving errors (7/16,7/16). All nonzero model branch probabilities are positive rationals. The witness has two first histories, two second symbols and two time layers; no universal size-minimality across all encodings is asserted.

A minimal within-witness repair is the one-bit provenance coordinate R_1(h)=1_{h=a}. It separates the two P-to-next-T kernel classes, supplies exact lumpability, and permits the full-history policy as a repaired statistic policy. LR alone cannot repair it because both histories have LR=1. No one-class refinement can recover (B1).

## Opposite witness; and why P-LUMP is not necessary for four scalars alone

Missing LR (reused from the prior iid source): at N=1 take P(a)=3/4,P(b)=1/4 and Q(a)=1/4,Q(b)=3/4. Collapse a,b into one terminal T-state. The continuation-kernel condition is vacuous (the only prior state is root). Deciding Q on a and P on b gives e_P=e_Q=3/4 and t_P=t_Q=1; a T-policy has e_P=r,e_Q=1-r and cannot agree.

Conversely, P-LUMP is *not* logically necessary for universal preservation of **only the four scalars**. Suppose P=Q on a positive finite history tree with compulsory first observation. Even if T-next kernels vary across the same T-fiber, any full policy has e_Q=1-e_P and t_P=t_Q=t∈[1,N]. A time-only Markov policy can stop at floor(t) or ceil(t), using one randomization to match E[tau]=t, and independently decide Q with probability e_P. Thus it matches all four observers for every original policy while generally failing to match T-indexed occupation flows. This explains the distinction between a reusable *sufficient lumpability criterion* and a general all-policy scalar equivalence characterization.

## Actual validation and typed BRC reuse

Executed exact verifier: EC40_verify.py, Python fractions.Fraction, with output EC40_REPORT.json. It verifies all branch probabilities, LR values, nonlumpability, (B1), Bayes-overlap 3/4, exact lower bound for 17 rational c values, attainment at c=1/2, and the horizon-one LR-erasure example. These are explicitly finite checks; the arbitrary-tree theorem comes from the algebraic proof. No physical heartbeat run, π/trigonometry, ordinary propagator or native residual attribution occurred.

**Reuse:** REUSE_APPLIED to definitions/ENTERPRISE_BRC_WEIGHTED_GLOBAL_SUBSTRATE_20260902.json (positive rational labeled branch carrier, multiplicity and ordered provenance) and the pinned iid LR-Markovization lemma. The genuinely new step is replacing iid-ness by LR plus *one-sided* history-dependent lumpability, proving Q-lumpability automatic, and isolating a sharp all-four observer obstruction. The four-scalar observer lease never authorizes erasure of path provenance for stronger future operations.

**Next problem:** find necessary/sufficient all-policy *four-scalar* equivalence for arbitrary finite P,Q and T without occupation-flow lumpability, perhaps via exact polytope projection and statistic refinement. Determine when the minimal residual is (LR, conditional future-kernel class) and when fewer coordinates suffice only for the four scalar functionals.
